newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall, uninspired by strong Coke, GM earnings.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall, uninspired by strong Coke, GM earnings.

text.p: Stocks fell Monday as Wall Street was uninspired by strong quarterly profits from market heavyweights such as Coca-Cola Co. and General Motors Corp.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 22.47 points at 6,369.22, continuing its retreat after tumbling 148 points Friday on concern about rising interest rates.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 2-1 on New York Stock Exchange volume of 217 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 3.67 points at 1,203.23.
Investors were cautious ahead of Tuesday's report on March consumer prices.
Stocks were rattled Friday by news that wholesale prices in March chalked up an unexpected 0.4 percent rise in the so-called core rate, which excludes often-volatile food and energy costs.
Now, Wall Street believes that the outlook for inflation and interest rates is pointing higher.
"The market started out with a decent tone, trying to get a technical rally, but it failed," said James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities.
Coca-Cola and General Motors, both components of the Dow index, posted first-quarter earnings that topped analysts' expectations. Coca-Cola rose 1-1/4 to 55, and General Motors was flat at 53.
Traders said there were concerns whether companies would be able to maintain strong earnings in the quarters ahead.
"I think the key is going to be on some of these bigger companies as they look forward past this quarter," Volk said. "The question is, does it hold up?"
Long-term interest rates edged higher. The Treasury's 30-year bond was off 3/32, and its yield rose to 7.18 percent from 7.17 percent on Friday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The 7.25 percent level on the 30-year bond is seen as a key point at which bonds become increasingly significant competition for stocks.

With the blue-chip Dow index now down about 10 percent from its record closing high set on March 11 at 7,085.16 and the bond yield running into technical resistance, stocks may be leveling out, said Robert Robbins, market strategist at Robinson-Humphrey.
"I think we're probably finding the beginning of a bottom" in the stock market, he said.
Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony, said he thought the Dow would fall to around 6,200 level before the current pullback is completed.
"We're anticipating we're probably going to have to go a little lower before we can get something going on the upside," he said.
Among individual stocks, USA Waste Services Inc. fell 3-1/4 to 32 after it said it was buying United Waste Systems Inc. in a stock swap valued at $1.7 billion. United Waste fell 5 to 32-5/8.
Patriot American Hospitality Inc. fell 2-1/8 to 20-1/8 after it said it agreed to acquire Wyndham Hotel Corp. and 11 hotels for $1.1 billion. Wyndham lost 1-3/4 to 27-7/8.

Novellus Systems Inc. sank 20-1/4 to 55-1/8 after the chip equipment maker said its first quarter book-to-bill ratio -- a key indicator of sales trends -- fell short of expectations and that it might face potential financial damage from a patent infringement lawsuit.
